I would like to apply braingraph on my diffusion data (currently in the form or connectivity matrices (for each subject) with number of streamlines between a set of regions.

Best,

vivian

messages.author: 28bb28f8fe8898a5
messages.subject: Re: [brainGraph-help] Input for structural connectivity analysis
parts:
Sure. Can you tell me:
* What atlas you are using
* How many subject groups you have
* What order the ROI's are in
* If all of your connectivity matrix files are in the same directory (or one directory per subject)

Chris

messages.author: 28bb28f8fe8898a5
messages.subject: Re: [brainGraph-help] Input for structural connectivity analysis
parts:
Ok, I am interested and hopeful in TrackVis working with brainGraph, so please tell me about your experience.
I think you should be able to follow the code I provided in the User Guide. You will possibly have to adjust specifically the "list.files" code to work with your directory structure (i.e., where you have placed the connectivity matrix files). Please let me know if you have any other questions.


P.S. Since TrackVis performs streamline (deterministic) tractography, I believe, then when you create the connectivity matrix objects in R, the command to use would likely be something like:

my.mats <- dti_create_mats(f.A, 'none', mat.thresh=thresholds,
                           sub.thresh=sub.thresh, inds=inds)

The reason "none" is chosen is because I have never seen a DTI graph theory paper that adjusts for e.g. ROI volume/area after streamline tractography, nor is there an associated "waytotal" value.
For the "thresholds" vector, you may want to choose something that would equal the number of streamlines to exceed; I have often seen a value of 1 or greater, and have seen 3 or greater. You can choose only one value or a range of values if you like.
Finally, for "sub.thresh" you may wish to choose "0" if you don't want a minimum percentage of subjects as the threshold. My default is "0.5", i.e. at least 50% of subjects must have a streamline count above "mat.thresh" for it to be accepted as a true connection.
